title: 3NF Exercises
description: Eliminate transitive dependencies to achieve Third Normal Form

data.text: Third Normal Form removes transitive dependencies where a non-key column depends on another non-key column. This further reduces redundancy and update anomalies.

data.title: 3NF violations
items: Employee table with department_name and department_budget
Product table with category_name and category_description
Order table with customer_name and customer_city

data.title: Transitive dependency
data.content: department_name and department_budget depend on department_id, not employee_id.
data.code:
CREATE TABLE employees (
  employee_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
  employee_name VARCHAR(100),
  department_id INT,
  department_name VARCHAR(100),
  department_budget DECIMAL(12,2)
);

data.title: 3NF solution
data.content: Move department data to its own table.

items.question: Is 3NF always desirable?
items.answer: Usually yes, but denormalization for performance is common after achieving 3NF.

items.question: How do I detect transitive dependencies?
items.answer: Draw a dependency diagram. If non-key A determines non-key B, and the key determines A, you have a transitive chain.

items.question: What about multi-valued dependencies?
items.answer: Those are 4NF concerns. Complete 3NF before tackling 4NF.

data.title: Summary
points: Identify transitive chains between non-key columns
Move dependent data to separate tables
Preserve foreign keys for referential integrity
data.takeaway: 3NF eliminates redundant non-key data, ensuring each fact appears in exactly one place.
